title: 3 tankers of the Iranian state-owned shipping company leave the Strait of Hormuz with 5 million barrels of oil
snippet: USA and Israel continue to attack Iran, Tehran strikes back. Iranian tankers cross the Strait of Hormuz despite conflict. Hundreds of Western ships remain blocked. All episodes for stock market and global economy in the live ticker. Iranian state shipowners exploit bottleneck in the Strait of Hormuz Friday, March 30, 10:40 a.m.: Three US-sanctioned tankers belonging to the Iranian state shipowner National Iranian Tanker Co (NITC) have passed through the Strait of Hormuz towards the Gulf of Oman. According to ship data service providers, they were loaded with around 5 million barrels of crude oil and sailed from the Persian Gulf on Sunday and Monday. title: China urges all parties to maintain security in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran says it has blocked it
snippet: China has called on all parties to the Middle East war to maintain security in the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil and gas route, and vowed to take measures to ensure its own energy security, AFP reported in Beijing. In addition, US Secretary of State Rubio told reporters on the 2nd yesterday that the United States will take action to deal with the situation of soaring energy prices caused by the US-Iran conflict, and revealed that US Treasury Secretary Bessant and Energy Secretary Wright will announce relevant plans on the 3rd today. Advertise Continue browsing the following AFP pointed out that the Strait of Hormuz is one of the most important waterways in the world, through which nearly a quarter of the world's maritime oil supply and a large amount of cargo transportation pass. The move comes after Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced the closure of the strait last Saturday, a move that has prompted several international shipping groups to suspend sailings in the waterway. "China urges all parties to immediately cease military operations to avoid further escalation of tensions, maintain the security of the Strait of Hormuz waterway, and prevent further impact on the global economy," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Mao Ning said at a regular press conference on Tuesday (March 3) Mao Ning further emphasized: 'Energy security is of great significance to the global economy... China will take necessary measures to ensure its own energy security.' China is a major buyer of Iranian oil, much of which needs to be transported through the Strait of Hormuz. title: Iran claims to close the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to 'set fire' to ships trying to cross it
snippet: A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guard official said on Monday that the Strait of Hormuz had been closed, threatening that if any ship crossed, Iran would 'set fire to those ships', according to what official media reported. The closure of this waterway in the Gulf, the world's most important oil export corridor, threatens to cause crude oil prices to rise sharply. However, Fox News quoted US Central Command (Centcom) as saying that the strait remains open. In statements reported by Iranian state media, Ibrahim Jabbari, senior advisor to the commander of the Revolutionary Guards, said: "The Strait of Hormuz is closed. If anyone tried to cross, the heroes of the Revolutionary Guard and the regular navy would set those ships on fire.'. This is the most explicit threat from the Iranian Revolutionary Guard to navigation in Hormuz since forces informed ships on Saturday of the closure of the export corridor. Earlier on Monday, the Revolutionary Guards announced that they had attacked an oil tanker allegedly linked to the United States in the Strait of Hormuz, as part of a series of strikes in response to the US-Israeli attack. The Guard said in a statement: "The oil tanker 'Athe Nova', one of the oil tankers belonging to the United States' allies in the Strait of Hormuz, is still burning after being targeted by two drones". The restrictions on navigation through the Strait of Hormuz came in response to US and Israeli strikes targeting Iran on February 28 aimed at toppling its regime, with US President Donald Trump offering the Iranians help in overthrowing the ruling clerics. Among those killed in the first strike was Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. snippet: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz closed amid escalation Iran has declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, with a senior Revolutionary Guards adviser warning that any ship attempting to pass will be attacked. The strait is the world’s most critical oil transit chokepoint, carrying more than 20 million barrels of crude and fuel daily. The threat has rattled global energy markets and raised fears of severe supply disruptions to Europe, the United States and Asia. Analysts warn that any sustained blockade could trigger sharp spikes in oil and shipping costs worldwide.
